lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1668: the row says what it is and what it does

Owner: "at workings to learn at a vendor, the things you buy need more than a
name, they need to tell you what they are and what they do on the button line. I
understand that if you tap on it you get the full detailed view but that's an
extra step. If I know it's an axe with electric base damage and it's a 2d10 then
it helps me choose faster."

⚠⚠ HE NAMED THE ONE BUY SURFACE THAT HAD NOTHING, and he was precise about which.
The ordinary offer rows have carried `kindLabel · rarity` plus a full stat line
for many OTAs. WORKINGS TO LEARN — the recipe list — printed the result's NAME,
its price, and the literal word "recipe". Comparing two workings meant opening
both and backing out of one, every time.

⚠ THE HEADLINE IS BUILT AT THE SOURCE, NOT PARSED AT THE ROW. Every branch of
itemPreview writes its own from values it already holds. The tempting shortcut —
have the caller slice stats[0] and regex "Damage: 2d10 (electrical)" back apart —
is how a screen eventually prints a weapon's durability where its damage belongs,
and it would have had to be repeated at every surface wanting the line. The
damage glyph is the one the combat button paints (OTA-1636) and the codex GLYPHS
tab explains (OTA-1667), so the shop and the fight teach one symbol.

⚠ AND THE INSTANCE HEADLINE FOLLOWS THE INSTANCE. A plain spread would have
carried the CATALOG's AC onto a piece whose AC was rolled — the row and the card
disagreeing about the same object, which is the OTA-1611 defect in a new place.

⚠⚠⚠ LOOT FINALLY SAYS WHAT IT IS FOR, folded in from the same message: "we need
to define what loot is in the inventory. It's just there, but what is it for?"

It already had a job and never said so — isForgeableLootReagent has fed the
Fusing Crucible since OTA-737, and OTA-1642 authored 86 enemy drops specifically
to keep that hopper full. ⚠ BUT THE ANSWER IS NOT ONE ANSWER, and a blanket label
would have been a lie: a drop named by ANY recipe is deliberately excluded from
the Crucible so fusing can never cannibalise crafting. lootPurposeLine reads those
same two predicates, so it says "crafting ingredient", or "Crucible fodder", or —
for the many things that are simply worth what a vendor pays — nothing at all.
The label and the bench's refusal cannot disagree. It renders on the vendor SELL
rows, which is exactly where the question gets asked, one tap before you sell
something the forge wanted.

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green (1129 suites / 11,711 tests).
